deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Deletion policy is an infrastructure lifecycle/operations setting (DELETE vs ABANDON vs PREVENT) controlling how Terraform manages destruction of the resource, not a control over exposure, access, or data protection. Enforcing PREVENT universally would hinder legitimate infrastructure cleanup and pipeline operations without directly mitigating a security risk.

network_endpoint_group.description: The network endpoint group these endpoints are part of.
network_endpoint_group.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the network endpoint group). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project determines resource ownership/location, similar to other identifier fields; it is not itself a security control.

zone.description: Zone where the containing network endpoint group is located.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

network_endpoints.description:
The network endpoints to be added to the enclosing network endpoint group
(NEG). Each endpoint specifies an IP address and port, along with
additional information depending on the NEG type.

network_endpoints.instance.description:
The name for a specific VM instance that the IP address belongs to.
This is required for network endpoints of type GCE_VM_IP_PORT.
The instance must be in the same zone as the network endpoint group.
network_endpoints.instance.rationale: A reference/pointer to another GCP-managed resource (the VM instance). Per the project's core rule, resource references are not themselves security controls.

network_endpoints.ip_address.description:
IPv4 address of network endpoint. The IP address must belong
to a VM in GCE (either the primary IP or as part of an aliased IP
range).
network_endpoints.ip_address.rationale: This IP must belong to an existing VM already within the GCP network, making it effectively a reference to that VM's networking configuration rather than an arbitrary external destination. Consistent with the project's reference rule, this is not itself a security control.

network_endpoints.port.description:
Port number of network endpoint.
**Note** 'port' is required unless the Network Endpoint Group is created
with the type of 'GCE_VM_IP'
network_endpoints.port.rationale: A routing parameter that pairs with the target address; it does not itself represent a security decision independent of which destination is being targeted.
